879.t: Crescent City Music School and St. Augustine band rehearsals
879.s: Saturday lessons stopped once St. Augustine's daily band rehearsals began; he spent three years there.
879.q: Uh, after I went to St. Augustine underneath the direction of, uh, Edward Hampton, uh, I discontinued my music lesson on Saturday because we, uh, every day, five days a week, we would rehearse the one hour in the morning. I had for now, half of the lunch period and about two hours after school.…

681.t: Tulane studies, Two Bits clubs and the 1932 Rose Bowl trip
681.s: Hirsch left Tulane architecture to play music, played Two Bits clubs and Honeysuckle Inn, had a drum shop and timpani, and went to the Rose Bowl with the Tulane band.
681.q: I lived, I lived too far uptown for it. I didn't live in that, live in that section. Where were you living then? On Napoleon Avenue. On Jefferson Avenue. In the uptown Tulane section, the university section. But, uh. You went to Tulane, didn't you? Mm-hmm. Two years, until I found out that if I…

635.t: Baseball and neglecting school for music
635.s: Foster tells of catching and hitting a home run, school friends who went on to be Bunk and Eddie, and why he did not want his grandchildren to study music in school.
635.q: W. G. And Eddie Sherry went there. W. G. There was a bunch of the guys went there, see. Because we used to, then I played baseball, see. I played baseball because I was catching for, I was pitching for my little team and I started catching. And we was playing at the Union Park, might know you. And…

820.t: Rene and Nappy in the Owls, picture and Benji White
820.s: Rene left for Tulane architecture and Nappy replaced him; a photo question and mention of interviewing Benji White.
820.q: No, no, no. Rene left to go to Tulane. He went to take up architecture and that's when Nappy took his place.

572.t: French at home and leaving St. Aloysius College
572.s: His parents spoke French; he was placed in a French class, was laughed at, tore up the book and left school.
572.q: Well, my mother, my mother and father spoke, uh, spoke French. Mm-hmm. And, and, they, they, they used to do a couple of French songs around the house, but, but I, I didn't, I didn't know too much about the French education.

194.t: Supporting himself by gambling; third-grade schooling
194.s: Records did not pay, so gambling supported his family; he left school after third grade at Arthur P. Williams School.
194.q: Yeah, Liberty I think. Perdita and Liberty. Yeah. They took up the whole block as well, you see. From Liberty to Franklin.

831.s: They discuss Eddie Edwards, who played violin for marching at Jackson School.
831.ch: Early bands and New Orleans musicians
831.q: Yeah. He used to play violin when I was going to school. He used to play the march for us to march up in the room on violin.

885.t: Playing shows six nights a week and leaving school
885.s: He left Booker T. Washington before graduating to earn money playing shows, sometimes seeing his teachers at the cabarets.
885.q: Yeah, yeah. I was waiting six nights a week. That's why I left. I didn't graduate from Booker T. I left school. Because I was making a little money at the time and it helped the family. My mother, she said I had a long talk with me and she didn't want to force me. You know, I had to play hockey and…

886.t: Schooling and no music in school
886.s: He attended Catholic and private schools, which had no music; he organized the Young Tuxedo band after the Depression.

196.t: Childhood on Lesseps (Lesion) Fields and schooling; no music study
196.s: He never studied music, learned Maple Leaf Rag from a French-named fellow, attended public school and grew up at 1325 Lesseps.

299.s: He attended grammar school with no band, and music reading was not taught to ordinary pupils.
299.q: Well...the kids they had in the band in school when I was going to school I don't think they could play without reading. Yeah.

302.s: No school music; he attended McDonogh No. 24 in Carrollton, possibly Mahalia Jackson's school.
302.q: Well, yeah, McDonough 24 was in Carlton, and I mean, we had to walk around about 18 blocks of school, man. I mean, there wasn't no such a thing as school buses, you know.

770.t: Women's school in Afghanistan and school supplies sent with Rod Alexander
770.s: Addie visits a girls' school in Kabul and arranges supplies to be carried by Rod Alexander's dance troupe.
770.q: Another after effect of this tour is when we were in Afghanistan I visited what's called the Women's Welfare Institute there, you know education facilities are quite primitive and practically non-existent the women over here. 639.t: Tulane dances and his own schooling
639.s: Wiggs says he studied at Tulane, Loyola and LSU, and Russell asks who ran the Saturday night dances.
639.q: Yeah, I took some work at Tulane. I never graduated from Tulane. I graduated from Loyola. And I took some work at LSU. I took some master's work at music at LSU. I graduated with a bachelor of music degree from Loyola.

306.t: Schooling in New Orleans; Professor Medard Nelson's school

81.t: Chicago schooling, becoming interested in music, and his mother's death
81.s: He went to Phillips high school in Chicago, was not at first interested in music, and his mother died in 1918.
81.ch: Porch interview and Jazz Train plans
81.q: Well, see, I can't remember exact ages, you know? When you get down to pinpointing ages and things, it's a little bit too much.

529.t: Ybor City, his night-working teachers and the school dance band
529.s: He describes his Spanish and Cuban Ybor City neighborhood, teachers who gigged at night, and bandmaster Mr. Rodriguez's school dance band that lacked a bass.

103.s: Asked about dance bands, Jones says he intended to be a surgeon and go to Switzerland at 16 until his mother said he could not go unless Calvin did.

473.t: Parents wanted college; Mrs. Allen's Tuskegee and Fisk connections
473.s: He told his parents after leaving; they wanted him in college, and Mrs. Allen could send promising pupils to Tuskegee or Fisk.
473.q: they wasn't for me -- after I got up, they wasn't for me playing music. They were for me going to college. Wanted me to go to school, you know.

13.t: Band captain, and band plus school orchestra
13.s: He gets into the band within a month, becomes captain after Allen graduates, and keeps playing violin in the orchestra.
13.q: All through high school. In fact, after the first semester, Charlie Allen was graduated. He was a 2nd Lieutenant. The 1st Lieutenant, the doctor took him off his instrument, on account of his health, and the captain graduated. And I wound up being captain of the band in one semester.
